category_title: Students with non-compliant behavior and difficulty accepting instructions or consequences
minimal_context: Garth is in the general classroom setting working on a teacher-selected spelling assignment involving writing definitions for 20 words.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Garth, it is time for spelling. I need you to write the definitions for these 20 words on your worksheet.

STUDENT: (Makes loud noises by tapping his pencil on the desk) I'm not doing definitions.

TUTOR: Please just get started on the words.

STUDENT: (Turns his back) Shut up, I don't care.

TUTOR: Garth, that is not appropriate. You need to follow the instructions or there will be consequences.

STUDENT: (Rips the spelling worksheet in half and knocks the textbook off the desk) No!

options.A: Provide a menu of five different spelling tasks (e.g., writing words three times, writing definitions) and allow the student to choose which task to complete.
options.B: Stop the spelling activity and explain the instructions for the definitions repeatedly until the student fully understands the assignment.
options.C: Agree with the student that he is having a rough time with the spelling assignment and pause the current activity.
options.D: Prompt the student to call on a neighbor, ask a friend, or poll the classroom for help with the spelling definitions.
